walkthroughs.body_html:
Practical Skills in Biology — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Practical Skills in Biology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Practical Skills in Biology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which scientist proposed 'omnis cellula e cellula' (all cells from pre-existing cells)?
options: Schleiden
Schwann
Virchow
Hooke

mcqs.q: The fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane was proposed in 1972 by:
options: Watson and Crick
Singer and Nicolson
Schleiden and Schwann
Margulis and Lovelock

mcqs.q: What is the main role of B-cells compared to T-cells?
options: B-cells produce antibodies (humoral response); T-cells coordinate the immune response and kill infected cells (cell-mediated response).
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
B-cells and T-cells both produce antibodies in equal amounts.
T-cells produce antibodies and B-cells kill infected cells.

mcqs.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
options: Insulin destroys glucose in the bloodstream so it cannot be used.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
It lowers blood glucose by causing cells (especially liver and muscle) to take it up and store it as glycogen.
Insulin raises blood glucose to give the body energy.

mcqs.q: How do vaccines protect you from a disease?
options: T-cells produce antibodies and B-cells kill infected cells.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Vaccines kill the pathogen if it ever enters the body.
They expose your immune system to a harmless form of the pathogen so memory cells form, allowing rapid response if exposed later.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Endosymbiotic theory”?
options: Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.
All living organisms are composed of cells; cells are the smallest unit of life; cells arise from pre-existing cells (Schleiden, Schwann 1838-39; Virchow 1858).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Eukaryote”?
options: Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
Phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins; selectively permeable (Singer & Nicolson 1972).
Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prokaryote”?
options: All living organisms are composed of cells; cells are the smallest unit of life; cells arise from pre-existing cells (Schleiden, Schwann 1838-39; Virchow 1858).
Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting diffusion; drives mitotic division.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Fluid mosaic model”?
options: Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
All living organisms are composed of cells; cells are the smallest unit of life; cells arise from pre-existing cells (Schleiden, Schwann 1838-39; Virchow 1858).
Phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins; selectively permeable (Singer & Nicolson 1972).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Surface area to volume ratio”?
options: Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.
Phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins; selectively permeable (Singer & Nicolson 1972).
As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting diffusion; drives mitotic division.
Cell without membrane-bound nucleus or organelles; DNA in nucleoid; includes bacteria and archaea.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cell theory”?
options: Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; includes protists, fungi, plants, animals.
Mitochondria and chloroplasts originated from free-living prokaryotes engulfed by ancestral eukaryotes (Margulis 1967).
As cells grow, volume increases faster than surface area, limiting diffusion; drives mitotic division.
All living organisms are composed of cells; cells are the smallest unit of life; cells arise from pre-existing cells (Schleiden, Schwann 1838-39; Virchow 1858).
